findings.claim: ADR-019 §3's bolded band claim "This row is the MAXIMUM at this count in the committed ledger" is false against the ledger this same commit ships, and the same bullet contradicts it twice below.
findings.evidence: ADR-019 §3 cites ts 20260828-052604 at 25.99s and calls it the maximum at 92 cases. history.jsonl holds 20260828-053100 at 26.07s (> 25.99) plus 20260828-054414 at 25.79. The grader's own maximum applies no dirty filter, so 26.07 is the ledger max. The same bullet then says "It is NOT necessarily the maximum at this count either" and "which of them is slowest is deliberately not retyped here". Ungraded: item 12 reads only the `(ledger max — <suite> at N cases: **X.XXs**)` marker form, which this sentence does not use. This is the R9 class recurring one round later.
findings.repro: List local invariant rows at total 92 -> 25.99 clean, 26.07 dirty, 25.79 clean.
findings.acceptance: The bullet states only what is true and what the rule needs (the cited row happened, is clean, derives the same ceiling as the ledger max), or names the actual maximum with item 12's graded marker.

R8's stated acceptance (strip only well-formed blocks, or a fence state machine) was not done. task-id-parse-boundary fixture 6 pins only the literal-\n prose line.

findings.acceptance: A fixture with a stray bare whole-line ``` above a genuine duplicate, watched red first, and either a fence state machine or a stripper that discards nothing when delimiters do not balance; the comment's stated ceiling names the real trigger. The info-string variant needs no fix — it already reports correctly.
